summary: Run 7 of M1-S03 — the fourth § 4 test-only repair, after reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 10 (S2-F-15). Run 10 answered § 0d's central UNVERIFIED question: Tier2WebhookFinalizerTest.cls (implementing System.FinalizerContext directly) compiles at API 67.0, and coverage rose to 86.8% — clear of the 75% floor. But 1 of 34 tests failed: transientFailureBelowAttemptCeilingIsRecordedRetryingAndReEnqueuedOnce. The org's real execution disproved § 0d's assumption that omitting Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() would stop the Finalizer's own re-enqueued Tier2WebhookQueueable from running — it ran to completion by the end of the test method regardless, and with no HttpCalloutMock registered anywhere in that method, its callout threw, was classified transient, and (landing at attempt=2, still below the ceiling) re-threw Tier2WebhookQueueable.execute's own line 340, uncaught. Fixed with one line — Test.setMock(HttpCalloutMock.class, new MockHttpResponseGenerator().withResponse(200, OK_BODY)) immediately before the finalizer.execute(...) call — plus a new OK_BODY constant and a corrected class header. The alternative offered (assert the enqueue without forcing execution) was not available: the org's own result already showed the job runs regardless of how the call is wrapped. All of the method's existing assertions remain valid because they read the database synchronously before the platform's later run of the re-enqueued job. No shipped class, no other test method, and no other file changed.
confidence_rationale: MEDIUM, up from run 6's more heavily caveated MEDIUM. Gate B: 0 unresolved symbols. Gate C check 3 (compile): this run cannot itself run a compile (still design-only, no target_org_alias), but the org's own run 10 result — handed to this run as an input, not produced by it — already confirms the file compiles and that 33 of 34 tests (all but the one this run fixes) pass, at 86.8% coverage. That resolves run 6's most serious named risk (S6-F-02, whether System.FinalizerContext is customer-implementable) in the affirmative. What keeps this at MEDIUM rather than HIGH is that no agent in this loop can re-run the dry run to confirm the fix actually turns the 34th test green — the fix is reasoned from the org's own diagnostic (the exact exception, the exact line, the exact method) and from the same skills already grounding this step, but it is unconfirmed by a fresh org run.

process_observations.observation: The org's diagnostic was specific enough (exact method name, exact throw site by line number, exact test counts) that the root cause followed directly from re-reading the shipped Tier2WebhookQueueable's own throw condition against each method's chosen attempt value — no speculation was needed to explain why exactly one of the two retry-branch methods failed and not the other.

This run's whole premise — that a test's assumption about Salesforce async test-execution semantics can be wrong even when it's carefully reasoned and explicitly flagged UNVERIFIED — is itself a data point: run 6 named the FinalizerContext-implementation question as the risk to watch, and it turned out fine; the actual defect was in an entirely different, unflagged assumption (that omitting Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() suppresses execution of a re-enqueued job). Flagging the risk you can name does not catch the risk you didn't think to name.

Whether Salesforce's real platform behaviour here — running a Finalizer's re-enqueued job to completion by the end of a test method even without Test.startTest()/Test.stopTest() — is documented anywhere official, or is specific to how this org's --test-level RunSpecifiedTests full test-class run works, is not established by anything in this run. It is treated as an empirical fact from this org's own result, not re-derived from a citation.
A fresh dry run with --test-level RunSpecifiedTests is the only way to confirm this fix actually turns the 34th test green and that coverage still clears 75% after it.
